title: Sensor Allowance Units and Sensor Counts by Model, Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program
content:
On every tier of the Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program the CGM supply allowance (A4239) is counted in billing units, one unit being one month's supply allowance, and the physical sensors shipped per 30 days follow each model's labelled wear period.

## Allowance and transmitter figures (every tier)

| Tier | Sensor allowance units per 30 days of supply | Dexcom G6 transmitter life (calendar days) | Larkfield ships its own replacement for a failed sensor |
|---|---|---|---|
| CGM Self-Pay Program | 1 | 90 | No |
| CGM Commercial HMO Program | 1 | 90 | No |
| CGM Commercial PPO Program | 1 | 90 | No |
| CGM Medicare Advantage Program | 1 | 90 | No |
| CGM Original Medicare Program | 1 | 90 | No |
| CGM Medicaid Program | 1 | 90 | No |

## Sensors per 30 days of supply, by model (identical on every tier)

| CGM model | Sensors per 30 days |
|---|---|
| Dexcom G7 | 3 |
| Dexcom G7 15 Day | 2 |
| Dexcom G6 | 3 |
| FreeStyle Libre 3 Plus | 2 |
| FreeStyle Libre 2 Plus | 2 |

## Notes

- The **sensor allowance units per 30 days of supply** are the A4239 billing units per 30 days of supply.
- The **transmitter life** is the Dexcom G6 transmitter life: one transmitter ships per this many days of supply within the A4239 allowance, at no extra unit.
- **Failed-sensor replacement**: the figure "No" on every tier means the manufacturer replaces a sensor that failed, errored or fell off before the end of its wear period directly; Larkfield ships no replacement of its own for it.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A hypothetical 60-day supply of a model that uses 2 sensors per 30 days contains two 30-day blocks; at 1 allowance unit per 30 days it is 2 billing units, and at 2 sensors per block it is 4 physical sensors.
